messages:
maya: heads-up — saw a spike in streaming token tail latency on gpu-pool-usw2 this morning. RPC deadline misses jumped ~3x between 04:18–04:28 UTC. graphs: https://dash.redwood/internal/gpupool/usw2?range=1h
liam: ugh. same window as the token-streaming 503s we saw yesterday?
carmen: i pulled a quick pcap from one of the affected nodes (gpu-rt-13). looks like a lot of out-of-order TCP segments + retransmits. pasted sample below:

maya: ```
14:18:04.123456 IP 10.20.5.13.54012 > 10.20.5.21.443: P 1:1410(1409) ack 1 win 65535 (DF)
14:18:04.123457 IP 10.20.5.13.54012 > 10.20.5.21.443: P 1410:2820(1410) ack 1 win 65535
14:18:04.123459 IP 10.20.5.13.54012 > 10.20.5.21.443: P 2820:4230(1410) ack 1 win 65535 (reordered)
14:18:04.123462 IP 10.20.5.21.443 > 10.20.5.13.54012: . ack 2820
14:18:04.123470 IP 10.20.5.21.443 > 10.20.5.13.54012: . ack 4230 (dup ack)
```

ajay: nic counters on that host?
liam: ethtool -S mlx5_core and mlx5e shows tx_fifo_errors and rx_out_of_order a few hundred in 10m on that NIC. queue_full == 0. offloads: GRO enabled, GSO enabled.
carmen: we also saw small bursts of larger MTU traffic (jumbo) from a contrail vxlan flow — maybe fragmentation/encap path mismatch. some nodes had MTU 9000, others 9216.
maya: timeline: token streaming service does continuous small writes for tokens (many small packets). If GRO is coalescing unevenly or NIC reorder due to TX ring scheduling + huge SNs from jumbo->nonjumbo, clients hit rpc deadlines since our server-side loop waits on in-order ACKs for small seqs.
liam: quick mitigation idea: disable GRO/GSO for the streaming interface on the affected hosts and push a kube daemonset to pin netdev settings. low-risk and reversible.
ajay: can we confirm RDMA is involved? some clusters have IB paths for cross-rack gpupools. tcpdump shows plain TCP over vxlan though. rdma device list is empty on gpu-rt-13. so likely kernel/net stack/encap issue.
carmen: on a repro host i ran: 

maya: ```bash
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_reordering=3   # kernel param, for testing
```

carmen: after disabling GRO/GSO we saw reorder rate drop to near-zero in the local pcap and tail RPC latency returned to baseline in the test canary (5% traffic).
liam: +1 to canary. ops-bot: can we schedule a daemonset to flip off GRO/GSO for gpu-pool-usw2 nodes and run for 30m before rolling cluster-wide? include a rollback in 15m if error rate spikes.
ops-bot: @liam scheduled: canary-daemonset/gro-disable -> targets: gpu-pool-usw2 (5%); window: 30m; rollback: 15m.

maya: also re: MTU, let's standardize to 9000 end-to-end for vxlan tunnels. i found a half-dozen hosts with 9216 causing fragmentation at the encapsulator which may re-chunk packets differently.
ajay: note: disabling GRO can increase CPU overhead — watch token-serving cpu (likely small) and egress pps. budget alert: put a 10% safety buffer on autoscale.
liam: logging ops: add short-lived tcp_info sampling for streaming connections so we can track reordering, rtt, and delivered. cg-run script:

liam: ```bash
python -c "import socket,struct; print('dump')"  # placeholder
```

carmen: SRE-oncall, can you watch the canary? if we see regressions we'll revert.
sre-oncall: watching. will alert if rpc_deadline_miss > 2x baseline or cpu delta > 15%.

maya: post-canary notes: after 20m the canary nodes show stable tail latencies and no reorder in tcpdump. we should:
- roll gro-disable daemonset to remaining gpu-pool-usw2 nodes over 30m
- start controlled roll to other regions (staging first)
- inventory MTU mismatches and bring to 9000 end-to-end
- open infra-ticket to work with provider on mlx5 fw/driver; might be scheduling bug on TX path

liam: agree. also create cost estimate for CPU delta while GRO off — add to the ticket.
ajay: created INF-3421 with actions + timeline. link: https://issues.redwood/INF-3421
carmen: small follow-up: test plan to re-enable GRO after driver/firmware patch — need perf baseline before/after.
maya: thanks all. great quick canary. :thumbsup:
liam: thanks — will follow up with a short postmortem doc and add kernel/tunables we changed to runbook.
sre-oncall: closing watch; will reopen if metrics breach.
